exposure: levonorgestrel emergency contraception (LNG EC) use in current cycle
previous or current use of intrauterine device
cohort: 144 women with ectopic pregnancy and 200 women with intrauterine pregnancies at a tertiary center in Gorakhpur, India, from April 2015 to March 2016.
finding: Several factors were associated with increased risk of ectopic pregnancy, including age >=30, previous deliveries, infertility, abortions, infections, and various surgeries; notably, levonorgestrel emergency contraception use was associated with increased risk, while previous ectopic pregnancy and IUD use were not.
mod_finding: Previous cesarean section was associated with an increased risk of ectopic pregnancy (OR = 1.446, 95% CI: 0.8408-2.486).
